$comment: Source of truth for this plan's requirements. status: exists (what the code does today, with file:line refs) | new (net-new work) | question (needs a decision) | decided | in-pr | shipped. steps are PR steps in README.md. The prototype's Spec drawer renders this file.

items.text: One 48px bar across the canvas and inspector. Today there is none: everything sits in rightSidebarActions at the top of the inspector rail.

Test: every top-bar control is 24px (design-system default) with 12/16 text, 6px radius, and edge padding sized to the content: 8px beside text, 4px beside a 16px glyph. The mode switch is a 24px segmented control (20px segments). Import and Share are 24px split buttons with a 20px chevron half. The bar stays 48px. Code today mixes 28px Figma selects with 32px toolkit sm buttons; 28 isn't on the 16/20/24/32 ramp.

Three columns with the route centred on the bar: left holds the mode switch, then device in Interact; centre holds back, forward, the route picker, and reload; right holds zoom, presence, Import, and Share.

Interact › Appearance: Light / Dark / System, next to the device picker. Today every inline screen iframe is pinned to colorScheme: "light" (DesignCanvas.tsx:7323, MultiScreenCanvas.tsx:12205), so no design previews dark. The picker sets that value instead; in Chromium an iframe's color-scheme drives prefers-color-scheme inside it, so designs with dark CSS follow with no changes. Design mode keeps today's light pin.

Zoom stays in the same spot in both modes and keeps its value. With 24px controls the route stays exactly centred from 1200px; below that the route takes the leftover middle (120–264px) and presence avatars hide.
In Design, the Screens panel picks the screen; routes and device sizes are Interact concepts.
Local app screens: Interact's route picker shows the localhost URL. Design shows Apply to source beside zoom (Scenario: Local app screen).
Right zone in both modes: Review changes when pending, presence, then Import and Share as split buttons.
Import: the button opens the Import dialog (today's DesignImportPanel sources); the chevron jumps straight to one source.
Share: the button opens the toolkit ShareDialog. The chevron holds Export: Download HTML, PNG, SVG, Figma SVG, ZIP, PDF, Copy agent prompt, and Publish app.

With the inspector showing, the bar's last column starts at the inspector's left edge: zoom ends 8px before it, and the avatars, Import, and Share sit over the inspector, leaving room for more people and agents. Without the inspector (Interact, narrow windows) the cluster sits together at the right.
Apply feedback (outline button, shown when the review queue has items) moves to the top of the Comments panel.
Review changes (pending node rewrites) moves to the top bar's right zone, same condition and menu.
Localhost link moves into Interact's route picker; Apply to source sits beside zoom in Design.
Play popover: Design Preview is what Interact does now, so it goes. Publish app (waitlist) moves to Share's dropdown.

Threads open on the canvas, attached to their element (Figma 1205:2267). Clicking a pill opens a 360px card beside it with the title bar (⋯, Resolve, Close), the messages, and a reply box. The Comments panel isn't needed for this.

Collapsed, a thread is an avatar pill at the element's top-right corner: up to three participants, plus the message count when there are replies (Figma annotation: “They collapse down to a small avatar pill”).
The card opens to the right of the pill and flips to its left when it would leave the canvas. Esc, ×, or clicking the canvas closes it; clicking the pill again toggles it.
The reply box expands on focus (accent border, emoji, @, image, send). Typing @ opens the mention picker of people and agents (Figma 1259:23236). A mention becomes a chip.
Agents reply in the thread with their brand mark and an Agent badge (Figma 1205:2713). Mentioning an agent starts a run; its answer lands in the same thread.
⋯ holds the Agent menu from Figma (Suggest changes, Reply in thread, Apply changes and resolve), then Copy link and Delete thread.
The Comment tool (C) or + in the Comments header: click an element and an empty card opens there with the box focused (Figma 1224:21402). Sending makes the thread and returns to Move.
The Comments panel is the finder: Open / Resolved / All, grouped by screen. A row opens its thread on the canvas, scrolling to the element and switching screens if needed.
Pixel grid: exists, but only on the overview canvas and automatically at 800% and up (shouldShowPixelGrid, canvas-math.ts:525; MultiScreenCanvas.tsx:10262).
Pixel grid becomes a toggle (on by default, still drawn from 800%), and the single-screen canvas (DesignCanvas.tsx) draws it too.
Snap to pixel grid: smart snapping exists for move, resize, and spacing (edges, centers, gaps within 6px; whole-pixel results via WHOLE_PIXEL_SNAP_STEP). Holding ⌘/Ctrl bypasses it while dragging.
Snapping gets an on/off toggle; ⌘/Ctrl still bypasses it per drag.

Layout grids ⌃G: the code's per-frame column/row grids (LayoutGridProperties) and their show/hide-all toggle (handleToggleLayoutGrids, DesignEditor.tsx:5279). Renamed from Figma's “Layout guidelines” to match the code. Press ⌃G in the prototype to see a 12-column grid.
Rulers: only the tick math exists (getRulerTicks, canvas-math.ts:514). The ruler UI is new work; off by default until it ships.
Multiplayer cursors: LiveCursorOverlay shows remote people and the agent's synthesized cursor, always on today.
Multiplayer cursors gets a toggle (on by default).
Comments ⇧C: exists.

A centred modal (760×640, shadcn Dialog) replaces today's 241px drawer pinned to the bottom of the editor (KeyboardShortcutsPanel.tsx:263), which also pushes the floating toolbar up (DesignBottomToolbar.tsx:406).
Title row is the shadcn Dialog header: title on the left, close on the right.

Left column (200px): search at the top, then the 13 categories from DESIGN_SHORTCUT_CATEGORIES. Clicking a category scrolls to it, and the current one follows the scroll. Right: one list with sticky category headings, name on the left, keycaps on the right, “or” between alternate bindings.
Search matches names, highlights the match, and narrows the categories to the ones with results; it has focus on open. The × clears it. Esc clears the search, then closes.

Rows come straight from DESIGN_SHORTCUTS and its designEditor.keyboardShortcuts labels, keycaps from formatShortcutKeycaps. Show assets stays out while its panel is behind SHOW_DESIGN_SECONDARY_LEFT_PANELS. Screen-only shortcuts carry a “Screen” tag.
Nudge amount (Small / Big px) moves from the drawer into the Cursor section, under Nudge and Big nudge.
Opens with ⌃⇧? (the registry's binding) and from the App menu: Help › Keyboard shortcuts and Preferences › Keyboard shortcuts.
Minimal UI (⇧⌘\) gets its own label, “Minimal UI”, instead of reusing “Show/Hide UI” (keyboard-shortcuts.ts:153).
Label for toggle-minimal-ui in the shortcuts window: keep “Minimal UI”?

areas.area: Menus and context menus (Figma Menus section 1432:3475)

items.text: App menu on the logo (1309:32918): Actions… ⌘K, then File (1693:1062), Edit (1693:1196), View (1693:1275), Preferences (1693:1330: Appearance…, Keyboard shortcuts), Help (1693:1371).
Design file menu on the file name (1309:32834), minus Move to folder… until folders exist. Zoom menu (1693:1945) with the view toggles.

Canvas context menus follow “Contextual action coverage” (1834:719), with each row's shortcut from CanvasContextMenu.tsx. Single layer: Edit with Agent…, Copy, Paste to replace, Copy/Paste as ›, Rename, Frame selection, Add auto layout, Create component, Hide, Lock, Arrange ›, Transform ›. Component instance: swaps the creation actions for Go to main component, Swap instance ›, Detach instance.

Multiple layers (1834:719; Shift-click to multi-select): Edit with Agent…, Copy, Paste to replace, Copy/Paste as ›, Group selection, Frame selection, Add auto layout, Boolean operations ›, Hide, Lock, Arrange ›, Transform ›. Boolean operations offers only Subtract (⌥⇧S), the one the code implements.

Empty canvas (1826:562 “No selection”): Paste here, Explore with Agent…, Show UI, Show comments. Layer row (1826:562): Copy, Rename (renames in place), Hide, Lock, Arrange ›, Transform ›, with LayersPanel's shortcuts.

Edit with Agent… is the highlighted first row. Clicking it opens the agent composer; its submenu is the Agent actions card (1826:562): Inspiration, Polish, Debug, Generate states, Make responsive, each with a one-line outcome.

Arrange › and Transform › use the code's commands: Bring to front ], Bring forward ⌘], Send backward ⌘[, Send to back [, Align left/right/top/bottom ⌥A/⌥D/⌥W/⌥S, Tidy up ⌃⌥T; Flip horizontal ⇧H, Flip vertical ⇧V, Swap fill and stroke ⇧X. (The Figma submenu card repeats instance rows as placeholders.)
Agents composer + is the “MVP Add context menu (prompt bar)” (2261:2104): Search…, Upload file, Attach Figma…, Reference a design…
Opens from the file menu and App menu › File › Version history. Today only the project menu opens it (DesignEditor.tsx:25688).

Today: a modal shadcn Sheet from the right, 92vw up to 640px (HistoryPanel.tsx:131), over a dimmed editor. List: accent dot, title, screen count, relative time. Titles are the stored labels (“Chat autosave”, “Before component delete”, “Before editor screen delete”, “Before restore”) or “After chat edit” for unlabeled chat versions. Pick “History: Sheet (today)” in the review strip to see it.
Today, a version opens a detail view in the same sheet: title, date · screen count, a two-column grid of screen thumbnails with file names, and a full-width “Restore this version”.

Versions are only created automatically: after an agent turn that edited the design (“Chat autosave”, server/plugins/agent-chat.ts:266), before screen and component deletes, and “Before restore” when restoring. In the prototype, Polish and agent mentions in comments autosave like the code does. Manual edits never create a version.

History mode (default in the prototype): Version history turns the inspector into a timeline and the canvas into the preview. The floating toolbar hides; canvas and layers are read-only; comment pins hide. The top bar shows “Version history”, “Viewing {version} · {time}”, zoom, Restore this version, and Done. Esc or Done exits back to the mode you came from.

Timeline: Current version on top (accent node), runs of autosaves (“Chat autosave”, “After chat edit”, “Before … delete”) collapse into “N autosave versions”, and named versions and restores stay their own nodes, joined by a vertical line. “Before restore” shows as “Restored version · saved before restoring”. Picking a version switches the canvas to it, and to its first screen if the current one isn't in that version.
Restore saves “Before restore”, replaces the design, and returns the timeline to Current version without leaving the mode.

Named versions: + opens a title and description form; the version saves with its author. The filter switches between All versions and Named versions only. Needs an additive created-by column on design_versions and a label/description save (today create-design-version only writes the pre-delete checkpoint).
Version history as a mode (the proposal) or today's HistoryPanel sheet? The prototype has both (review strip › History).

In code: TokensPanel.tsx with index-design-tokens, apply-design-token-edit, preview-design-token-edit, and import-design-tokens. It's hidden by a build-time env switch, VITE_SHOW_DESIGN_SECONDARY_LEFT_PANELS (pages/design-editor/types.ts:36), not a runtime feature flag; the same switch hides Assets, Tools, and Code. Its strings are raw literals (“localized when this feature is finalized”).

Ships behind a Labs flag: add a design.tokens lab in shared/labs.ts (like DESIGN_TWEAKS), read it with useLab for the rail item, and list it in Settings › Labs. Tokens leaves the VITE_SHOW_DESIGN_SECONDARY_LEFT_PANELS build switch; Assets, Tools, and Code keep it. Toggle “Labs: Tokens” in the review strip.

Tokens becomes a rail item (after Agents) and a left panel on the shared 16px row strip: groups Colors, Typography, Spacing, Radius, Shadows & Effects, Other, each collapsible. A row is swatch or type glyph, name, and value; hovering shows the source (file or design system).
Click a row to edit its value in place (Enter saves, Esc cancels). The color swatch opens the system color picker. Edits restyle the canvas live, like apply-design-token-edit.

Two header actions replace today's one create popover. + Add token is a Nova menu of token kinds in the panel's group order: Color · Font family, Font weight, Font size, Line height, Letter spacing · Spacing, Container, Breakpoint, Radius · Shadow, Opacity. A kind adds a draft row at the end of its group with the kind's prefix and a starting value (Font size → --font-size-, 16px); type the name, Enter moves to the value, Enter or clicking away saves, Esc cancels.

Why: today's Add one token is a CSS-variable field and a value field that defaults to #000000, and classifyVar (actions/import-design-tokens.ts:130) guesses the group from the name and value. Picking the kind first stores the type explicitly, so the token lands in the right group without reordering.

Container, Breakpoint, and Opacity are new kinds (the code's types are color, typography, spacing, radius, shadow, motion, other). Spacing becomes “Spacing & Layout” to hold Container and Breakpoint; Opacity lands in Shadows & Effects.

Import (Tabler download icon, the arrow into a tray) is a Nova menu like +, and each item imports straight away with a toast of what changed: Paste Figma link, DTCG file…, CSS or Tailwind file…, Code folder…, Paste from clipboard, then Generate from design. Each source names what it reads. It replaces Import a set from text, from a file, and from a folder; the same parser runs underneath, and DTCG is detected by content.

Paste Figma link reads the file link you copied in Figma from the clipboard, so there's no field to fill in; without one, the toast says to copy it first. It reads the file over Figma's REST API with the workspace's Figma connection (FIGMA_ACCESS_TOKEN, the same one frame import uses): color, text, and effect styles on every plan, and variables when the account has Enterprise (FIGMA_INTEROPERABILITY.md:53); otherwise the toast says variables need Enterprise. Paste from clipboard routes a Figma link here too. In code this is a figma source on import-design-tokens.

Figma's MCP (mcp.figma.com) is in core's MCP catalog but only accepts approved clients, so Design can't connect to it yet. Paper's route works today: an external agent (Claude Code, Codex) connects to both Figma's MCP and Design's own MCP server (every Agent-Native app mounts one, see mcp-protocol docs), reads get_variable_defs, and calls import-design-tokens. The design-systems skill already tells the agent to use Figma MCP tools when they're connected.

Generate from design (the Import menu and the empty state) starts a generate-tokens agent skill in the Agents panel: it reads the screens, names tokens by role, merges near-duplicates, and proposes the set for Apply. It replaces Import from current design, whose regex extraction becomes the skill's first step.
Export: the prototype puts Download tokens (DTCG) in Share › Export with the other downloads, shown while the Tokens lab is on. Keep it there, or give the panel its own export?

Changed from the code panel to match the shell: the header is the token count, then Search, Import, and + (Refresh goes away). Search swaps in for the whole header line as a focused 32px field with a ⌘F hint; Clicking away, ×, or Esc dismisses it and clears the query; clicking a result row keeps it. The code's Layers search already works this way (searchOpen in LayersPanel.tsx:886). Group headers drop their counts and uppercase labels; rows are 32px (code: 28px).

⌘F searches the region you last clicked or focused: Tokens, Comments, and Agents open their own search; the File panel, the canvas, and the inspector open Layers search, which is what ⌘F (find, handleFindLayers) does everywhere today. As in useDesignHotkeys, ⌘F stays native inside text fields. In code, onFind asks the focused panel for a focusSearch handle before falling back to layersPanelRef.

Storage today: a design's own tokens are CSS custom properties in each screen's :root; edits and imports land in designs.data.tweakSelections, a flat { "--var": value } map shared with Tweaks; brand kits and design systems keep a custom BrandKitToken[] (name, cssVar, value, type, group, source) plus fixed fields in design_systems.data. Localhost and Fusion source write-back is “planned”; no file is written. Nothing reads or writes DTCG.

Store tokens as DTCG (Design Tokens Format Module 2025.10): nested groups, $value, $type, $description, aliases like {color.primary}, colors as { colorSpace, components, alpha, hex } and dimensions as { value, unit } in px or rem, and Agent-Native data (source, cssVar override) under $extensions. CSS variables become derived output (color.primary → --color-primary), not the source of truth.

DTCG in the panel: Import › DTCG file… reads .tokens and .tokens.json files; the other imports detect DTCG JSON too. Groups inherit $type; {alias} and $ref references resolve; colors, dimensions, durations, font families and weights, cubic-béziers, and shadows convert to CSS. A com.agent-native.cssVar extension keeps the variable name, otherwise the path becomes it (color.primary → --color-primary). Share › Export › Download tokens (DTCG) writes the same shape back.
Keep the Container, Breakpoint, and Opacity token kinds in the + menu, or trim it to the types the code has (color, typography, spacing, radius, shadow, motion, other)?

Figma 1057:1991 (Toolbar section 1098:17334), 252×48: Move▾, Frame▾, Pen▾, Comment, Agent▾. Text and the Shape tool fold into Frame's Insert menu. Interact: Interact, Comment, Agent▾. Annotate (Labs): Draw▾, Comment, Agent▾.
Split buttons: 32×32 tool, 1px gap, 16×32 chevron, separate hover per half, chevron filled while its menu is open. Comment has no chevron.
The toolbar is pinned 8px above the canvas viewport's bottom edge (today 16px), whatever the page height. The canvas keeps 64px of bottom scroll room so the last content can clear it.

Select menu: Move V, Hand tool H, Scale K. Insert menu on Frame: Frame F, Text T, Screen, Image/video…, then Rectangle R, Line L, Arrow ⇧L, Ellipse O, Polygon, Star. Picking an option swaps the tool's icon.
Pen menu: Pen P and Draw ⇧Y. Draw is Annotate, so it only shows with Labs: Annotate on. With the lab off, Pen keeps its chevron and a one-item menu so the toolbar stays 252px.

Agent: the button opens the Agents panel with the composer focused and the selection attached. The chevron opens the Agent menu: Inspiration ⇧I, Debug ⇧S, Polish S. A skill starts a chat run in the Agents panel.

Shortcuts come from DESIGN_SHORTCUTS (keyboard-shortcuts.ts): Move V, Hand tool H, Scale K, Frame F, Text T, Image/video ⇧⌘K, Rectangle R, Line L, Arrow ⇧L, Ellipse O, Pen P, Draw ⇧Y, Comment C. Screen, Polygon, and Star have none. Skills keep the Figma Agent menu keys (Inspiration ⇧I, Debug ⇧S, Polish S), which nothing in code uses yet. The mode switch has no single-key shortcut because I is the eyedropper. ⌘K stays with Actions… in the App menu.
Annotate becomes a Labs flag in shared/labs.ts, read with useLab like DESIGN_REVIEW_TOOLS_LAB. Off: two modes, no Draw. On: the Annotate segment and Draw return, with today's Draw overlay.

The rail is 56px (Figma's width; the code is 64px today). Each item follows Figma's rail button: full width, a 20px icon in a 32px box, the 11/16 label under it truncating with an ellipsis, and the full name in a tooltip to the right after 500ms. Clicking the active item collapses its panel, as the code's onPanelChange(active ? null : panel) already does, so items carry aria-expanded. Footer controls stay 16px.

The rail label for comments is “Threads” (43px at 11px; “Comments” is 56px and truncated in the 56px rail). The code already calls them threads (“Only your threads”). The panel header counts threads; search and filter labels stay the code's “comments” strings.
Comments is a rail item with an open-thread count.
Logo opens the App menu from Figma: Actions… (⌘K), File, Edit, View, Preferences, Help, each a submenu.
File shows Screens and Layers. Agents shows Recent chats, with the composer pinned at the bottom and the selection attached as context.

Inside a chat, a back chevron before the title returns to the chat list, and the title menu starts with All chats, the toolkit AgentPanel header item (agentPanel.allChats) that opens the history view. The title menu lists recent chats to jump between.

Skills start from the composer: typing / opens the toolkit's mention picker (MentionPopover, default density) listing the app's skills (use-skills / slashSkills): icon, name, and the description truncated with the full text in a tooltip; ↑↓ and Enter or Tab pick, Esc closes. Picking inserts an inline skill chip (skillReference) and you keep typing instructions; Enter runs the skill with them. This is the shared PromptComposer behavior today. The panel's Skills section is gone; the toolbar's Agent ▾ menu still lists skills with ⇧I, ⇧S, and S.
Apply feedback (n) sits at the top of the Open list and starts the agent run. The rail footer's speech-bubble icon goes away.

Today the list renders inside the inspector (EditPanel.tsx:3189, :3251) and a pin opens the inspector's Comments tab (DesignEditor.tsx:18183). Agent context moves from inspectorTab: comments to leftPanel: comments in use-navigation-state.ts.

The rail footer's account control is the toolkit AccountMenu / OrgSwitcher compact trigger: a 24px avatar (tooltip: name and organization), not Figma's briefcase. Its menu opens above the avatar, start-aligned, 6px away, at least 248px wide (side="top" align="start" sideOffset={6}): email, organizations, invitations, Create organization, Settings, Usage, Log out. Design passes no utilityLinks, so Get apps and extensions doesn't show.

Every left panel shares one header: a label (the count or the chat switcher), then Search, Filter, and +. Only the File panel keeps the hide-panel button; the others collapse from their rail item (click the active one) or ⌘\. Search swaps in for the line as a focused field; clicking away, ×, or Esc dismisses it and clears the query, while clicking a result row keeps it. Filter uses Tabler filter-2 (three shortening lines) in every panel, replacing IconAdjustmentsHorizontal in ReviewCommentsPanel, and turns accent while any filter is on.

Comments: search and filters are the code's ReviewCommentsPanel (today used in review and Present): search matches every message's text; Filter comments holds Show resolved comments, Only your threads, Unread, Only current page, Sort by date or unread, and Mark all as read. It replaces the prototype's Open / Resolved / All picker; the header shows the count.

Agents: search covers chats (title and messages, core's searchThreads). The filter menu holds Sort by date (core's order: pinned first, then newest updatedAt) and Sort by unread, then Pinned only and Show archived chats, from the thread's pinnedAt / archivedAt. Unread is new: a dot marks a chat whose run finished after you last opened it, and core keeps no read state for chats today, so it needs a per-thread last-read time. Pinned chats show a pin, archived ones are dimmed. Search and Filter show on the panel's home list, not inside a chat.

Agents use Tabler sparkles everywhere the robot was: the rail item, the toolbar's Agent button, Edit with Agent… and Explore with Agent…, and the agent actions. The Polish skill moves to wand so it doesn't share the agent mark.
Should the Agents panel keep the code's 320px minimum width (DesignEditor.tsx:26516, AgentChatSurface) when every other left panel starts at 232px?
Update the Figma Navigation page note on the collapsed rails (646:5188, 1850:8474): it still says 72px; the rail is 56px.
File name opens the Design file menu from Figma: Rename, Duplicate, Version history, Save as template…, Export…, Move to trash. Move to folder… is hidden until folders exist.
Under the name, a ghost button reads “Designs” and goes to /home. No arrow: the label sits flush with the file name, and the hover fill extends 4px past it.
Move to folder… is hidden until designs have folders.
32px rows, 40px headers. One strip: 16px inset, 24px spacer per depth, 16px disclosure slot (empty on leaves), 8px, 16px icon, 8px, name. Press G to see the spacers.

The left panel resizes from its right edge in 8px steps: 240px default, 232px minimum (the first 8pt width at or above the 227px Figma spec), 416px maximum. Double-click resets to 240px; arrow keys nudge 8px (Shift 40px). Code today defaults to 280px and clamps 220–420px (DesignEditor.tsx:2273, :26513).
No tab row. The inspector starts at the selection header and only does properties. Comments move to the left rail.
Every section is a 40px header and rows on the 88 / 8 / 88 / 8 / 32 grid; fields are 12px label, 4px, 24px control.
Sections with nothing in them (Stroke, Effects) drop the chevron and keep its space, so titles line up.
Interact and Annotate hide the inspector; the canvas takes the width.

Every Agent-Native app already mounts a remote MCP server at /mcp (OAuth 2.1; calls run as the signed-in user, under the design's sharing rules). Unlike Paper's local desktop server, a designer's link works from any machine.

Copy link to selection is the first item in Copy/Paste as › on a layer or multi-selection, and sits after Copy on instances and layer rows; the empty canvas gets Copy link to screen. Links carry scope: /design/agent-native-web?screen=home&node=hero-title. Opening one selects the layers and zooms to them.

Share is a popover under its button (the toolkit ShareButton) with Content's tabs, People and Agents (peopleTabLabel / agentsTabLabel, DocumentToolbar.tsx:1428). Both panes share one grid cell, so switching tabs never resizes it. Density matches the app: 24px controls, 32px rows, 12/16 text. No Social or Embed rows, and no password or expiry, which only Clips has.

People: an invite field with the role inside it (Viewer ▾) and a send button, Who has access (owner, people with role menus), general access with the toolkit's three options (Only people with access can view, Anyone in your organization can view, Anyone signed in with the link can view), then Copy link.

Send to › sits under Edit with Agent… on layers, instances, and multi-selections (scope: the selection) and under Explore with Agent… on the empty canvas (scope: the screen). It lists one shared set of destinations, grouped Agents, Apps, and Channels, then Copy agent prompt and Manage destinations… (Settings › Integrations). Share › Agents shows the same set.

Where each group comes from, and its payload. Agents are the toolkit deep links (buildAgentShareDeepLink: Claude, Claude Code, Codex), always shown since nothing detects installed apps; the prompt carries the scoped link and the MCP URL, and the agent reads the context over the Design MCP. Apps are the workspace's other Agent-Native apps (useOrgSwitcherAppLinks, workspace runtime only); Design calls the app over A2A (call-agent) with an objective and the scoped link, then opens the result with /_agent-native/open. Channels are messaging channels in the on state (list-messaging-channels); posting the scope's screenshot and link is new, since channels only receive today.

Share › Agents: the scope row (Selection, the screen, This design), Copy agent prompt, Open in Claude / Claude Code / Codex, Send to Slides / Content, Post to #design-review, and MCP server settings (Settings › MCP server, /settings/mcp, where people connect Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, and other clients). It replaces the earlier Connect an agent link, which didn't say where it went.

Needs new read-only MCP tools on Design's connector allowlist: get-design-context { url } (that scope's HTML/CSS, tokens as DTCG, screenshot URL, layer tree, open comments, design system), get-design-tokens { url }, and get-design-screenshot { url }. Today every read action takes an id and nothing parses a Design URL.
If the design isn't visible to the engineer's org, should the tab offer to switch General access to Anyone in the org can view, or only say who can open it?
Rename Share › Agents › MCP server settings to Connect AI apps…, so the row says what the person gets rather than the mechanism?

Settings is the toolkit SettingsShell, a full page at /settings/:page: a 252px rail with Back to Design, Search settings (/ to focus, Enter opens the first hit), and groups Account · Design · Connections · Agent · Organization, then an 824px column under a sticky 60px header with the page's action. Pages, order, labels, and visibility come from core-pages.ts plus what templates/design/app/routes/settings.tsx passes (Labs, MCP about, What's new, Creative context while its lab is on, Agent Observability for owners and admins). Notifications and Extensions don't show in Design.

Entry points in the prototype: the account menu's Settings (⌘,) opens Profile and Usage opens Usage, as OrgSwitcher does; ⌘, works anywhere; Share › Agents › MCP server settings opens MCP server; Send to › Manage destinations… opens Integrations. Back to Design returns to the editor.

Labs adds Tokens and Annotate rows (marked New) for the two labs this redesign proposes; flipping them here changes the editor, like the review strip's Labs switches. Creative context's switch shows or hides its page, as in the code.

Found while mapping it: Design System setup links to /settings/integrations#secrets:GITHUB_TOKEN (DesignSystemSetup.tsx:1350), an anchor nothing on Integrations matches; it probably belongs on API keys.

The app theme is a menu, not a setting: App menu › Preferences › Theme › Light, Dark, System theme (checked), using the code's next-themes setTheme. Today it's only the command menu's Toggle theme (root.tsx:127), which flips light and dark. It replaces Figma's Appearance… item. Interact's Appearance control stays separate: it sets the previewed design's color scheme, not the editor's. Preferences also gets Nudge amount…, a small dialog for the code's Small nudge (1px) and Big nudge (10px), clamped to 1–1000px.
